quests.question: The rich ___ not always happy.
quests.hint: 'The + adjective' used as a noun always refers to a group - plural verb.
quests.explanation: When 'the' precedes an adjective to refer to a group of people ('the rich', 'the elderly', 'the young'), it is always treated as plural. 'The rich are not always happy'.

quests.question: The elderly ___ often overlooked in discussions about technology.
quests.hint: 'The elderly' refers to elderly people as a group - plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'The elderly' means 'elderly people in general'. Like 'the rich' and 'the poor', it is always plural: 'the elderly are often overlooked'.

quests.question: The injured ___ rushed to hospital after the accident.
quests.hint: 'The injured' refers to multiple injured people - plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'The injured' refers to injured people collectively and is always treated as plural. 'The injured were rushed to hospital'.

quests.question: The unemployed ___ facing increasingly difficult conditions.
quests.hint: 'The + adjective' referring to a group of people is always plural.
quests.explanation: 'The unemployed' means 'unemployed people in general' and is always plural: 'the unemployed are facing difficult conditions'.

quests.question: The unexpected ___ often what makes a story memorable.
quests.hint: 'The unexpected' referring to an abstract concept is singular.
quests.explanation: When 'the + adjective' refers to an abstract idea rather than a group of people ('the unexpected', 'the unknown', 'the impossible'), it is singular: 'the unexpected is what makes a story memorable'.

quests.question: The unknown ___ both exciting and frightening at the same time.
quests.hint: 'The unknown' as an abstract concept is singular.
quests.explanation: 'The unknown' refers to the concept of things not yet known - an abstract singular idea. 'The unknown is both exciting and frightening'.

quests.question: Both the plan and its execution ___ flawed.
quests.hint: Two things joined by 'both…and' always form a plural subject.
quests.explanation: 'Both…and' always creates a plural compound subject. 'Both the plan and its execution were flawed' - the verb must be plural.

quests.question: Both speed and accuracy ___ essential in this role.
quests.hint: 'Both…and' creates a plural subject - always use a plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'Both…and' always creates a plural subject. 'Both speed and accuracy are essential' - even if each item on its own would be singular.

quests.question: Neither the design nor the functionality ___ impressive.
quests.hint: Both subjects after 'neither…nor' are singular - what does that tell you about the verb?
quests.explanation: When 'neither…nor' joins two singular subjects ('the design' and 'the functionality'), both are singular, so the verb is singular: 'was impressive'.

quests.question: Neither the design nor the features ___ impressive.
quests.hint: With 'neither…nor', look at the subject closest to the verb.
quests.explanation: With 'neither…nor', the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it. 'The features' is plural, so 'were impressive' is the correct choice.

quests.question: Neither the features nor the design ___ impressive.
quests.hint: The subject right before the verb is 'the design' - is it singular or plural?
quests.explanation: The subject nearest to the verb is 'the design', which is singular. With 'neither…nor', the verb always follows the nearer subject: 'was impressive'.

quests.question: Both the manager and the CEO ___ aware of the problem.
quests.hint: Two people joined by 'both…and' - how many subjects does that make?
quests.explanation: 'Both…and' creates a compound subject from two singular items. Even though 'the manager' and 'the CEO' are each singular, joining them with 'both…and' makes the subject plural: 'were aware'.

quests.question: The new director, along with her team, ___ restructuring the department.
quests.hint: The main subject is 'the new director' (singular) - 'along with her team' is parenthetical.
quests.explanation: 'Along with her team' is a parenthetical phrase and does not change the subject. The main subject is 'the new director', which is singular: 'is restructuring'.

quests.question: The new director, as well as her predecessors, ___ faced this challenge before.
quests.hint: The main subject is 'the new director' (singular) - 'as well as her predecessors' is parenthetical.
quests.explanation: 'As well as her predecessors' is a parenthetical addition. The main subject is 'the new director', which is singular. 'The director has faced this challenge before'.

quests.question: The CEO, together with the board members, ___ announced the merger.
quests.hint: The main subject is 'the CEO' (singular) - 'together with the board members' is parenthetical.
quests.explanation: 'Together with the board members' is parenthetical. The real subject is 'the CEO', which is singular. 'The CEO has announced the merger'.

quests.question: The proposal, not the individual amendments, ___ rejected by the board.
quests.hint: The main subject is 'the proposal' (singular) - the contrasting phrase doesn't change that.
quests.explanation: When a contrasting phrase introduced by 'not' follows the subject, the verb still agrees with the main subject. 'The proposal' is singular: 'was rejected'.

quests.question: The amendments, not the main proposal, ___ rejected by the board.
quests.hint: The main subject is 'the amendments' (plural) - the contrasting phrase doesn't change that.
quests.explanation: The main subject is 'the amendments', which is plural. 'Not the main proposal' is a contrasting phrase that doesn't change the agreement. 'The amendments were rejected'.

quests.question: The company, including all its subsidiaries, ___ now under investigation.
quests.hint: The main subject is 'the company' (singular) - 'including all its subsidiaries' is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'Including all its subsidiaries' is a modifier, not a second subject. The main subject is 'the company', which is singular: 'is under investigation'.

quests.question: There ___ growing evidence that the vaccine is effective.
quests.hint: The real subject is 'growing evidence' - 'evidence' is uncountable (singular).
quests.explanation: In 'there is/are' sentences, the verb agrees with the real subject. 'Evidence' is uncountable and singular, so 'there is growing evidence' is correct.

quests.question: There ___ many reasons why this approach might fail.
quests.hint: The real subject is 'many reasons' - 'reasons' is plural.
quests.explanation: The real subject is 'many reasons', which is plural. 'There are many reasons' - the verb agrees with the noun after 'there'.

quests.question: There ___ considerable debate about the right course of action.
quests.hint: The real subject is 'considerable debate' - 'debate' used as uncountable here is singular.
quests.explanation: 'Debate' used as an uncountable noun (meaning 'discussion') is singular. 'There is considerable debate' - singular verb with uncountable noun.

quests.question: There ___ a number of factors contributing to this outcome.
quests.hint: 'A number of factors' means 'several factors' - plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'A number of factors' = 'several factors'. In 'there is/are' sentences, the verb agrees with 'a number of factors', which is treated as plural. 'There are a number of factors'.

quests.question: There ___ the possibility that the project will be cancelled.
quests.hint: The real subject is 'the possibility' (singular).
quests.explanation: The real subject is 'the possibility', which is singular. 'There is the possibility that the project will be cancelled'.

quests.question: There ___ various approaches to solving this kind of problem.
quests.hint: The real subject is 'various approaches' (plural).
quests.explanation: The real subject is 'various approaches', which is plural. 'There are various approaches to solving this problem'.

quests.question: The key to success in this industry ___ adaptability and resilience.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the key to success' (singular) - the complement doesn't control the verb.
quests.explanation: 'The key to success' is the subject, not 'adaptability and resilience'. With linking verbs, the verb agrees with the subject, not the complement. 'The key is adaptability'.

quests.question: Adaptability and resilience ___ the key to success in this industry.
quests.hint: The subject is 'adaptability and resilience' (plural compound) - not the complement.
quests.explanation: Now 'adaptability and resilience' is the compound subject, making it plural. 'Adaptability and resilience are the key to success'.

quests.question: The best solution ___ often the simplest one.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the best solution' (singular) - the complement 'the simplest one' doesn't control the verb.
quests.explanation: The subject is 'the best solution', which is singular. With linking verbs, the verb always agrees with the subject: 'the best solution is the simplest one'.

quests.question: The main concern of investors ___ whether the project will deliver returns.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the main concern' (singular) - 'of investors' is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The main concern' is the singular subject; 'of investors' tells us whose concern it is. 'The main concern is whether the project will deliver returns'.

quests.question: The concerns of investors ___ well documented in this report.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the concerns' (plural) - 'of investors' is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The concerns' is the plural subject; 'of investors' is a modifier. 'The concerns are well documented' - plural subject, plural verb.

quests.question: The group of researchers who published the study ___ from three different countries.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the group' (singular collective) - relative clause is descriptive.
quests.explanation: 'The group' is the subject - a singular collective noun. The relative clause 'who published the study' describes the group but doesn't change agreement. 'The group is from three countries'.
